$$

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{3}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}+{e}^{x/3})\text{d}x & =\int \frac{3}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}\,\text{d}x+\int {e}^{x/3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3\int -\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}\,\text{d}x+\int {e}^{x/3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x+3{e}^{x/3}+C \\  & =3(-\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x+{e}^{x/3})+C\end{aligned}
$$

$$
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cotangent function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int -\frac{2x}{{x}^{3}-x}\,\text{d}x & =\int -\frac{2x}{x({x}^{2}-1)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int -\frac{2}{{x}^{2}-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2}{1-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\pi }{e-e{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{\pi }{e(1-{x}^{2})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{\pi }{e}\int \frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{\pi }{e}\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
